findings.summary: The negation list cancels any criterion that contains a common word like 'skipped', 'omitted', 'excluded', 'deferred' or 'not covered', even when the request part itself uses that word. Correct readings would be refused, and the refusal text does not let the reader see why.
findings.evidence: Decision 6: 'A criterion holding any CRITERION_NEGATION phrase covers nothing.' The list includes skipped, omitted, excluded, deferred, postponed, not covered, left out and not part of. In this repository these are everyday words for what is being built (skipped checks, excluded paths, omitted fields, deferred parts). Take a part '(2) Report skipped checks in status'. Its natural criterion 'status lists skipped checks' contains 'skipped', so it covers nothing, and the reading is refused. This job's own reading shows the effect: criterion 2 holds 'as a follow-up' and criterion 3 holds 'deferred', so 2 of its 8 criteria would cover nothing. Step 3's error says only that the part is absent or in out_of_scope. It never says that a named criterion was ignored because of a word. On the one re-read (reading.rs:738-759) the reader is likely to write the same criterion again and be refused again. These refusals also land in the replay window. The replay holds a candidate whose newly refused share is above 15% (replay.rs:161, 296-308), and most of that window is generated requests with Acceptance bullets (steward.rs:581-585). Fix: Ignore a negation phrase whenever the part's own text contains it, so the request's vocabulary never cancels its own criterion. Outside the marker tier, treat only job-scope phrases (DEFER_PHRASES plus 'out of scope'/'out-of-scope') as cancelling a criterion. Make the error name every criterion that was ignored and the phrase that caused it. Add corpus cases: a part containing 'skipped' or 'excluded' with a criterion using that word is accepted, and 'The timeout test is deferred' still does not cover.

findings.summary: The title line of a generated root-cause request repeats the cause text, but it is not on the skip list. An enumeration in the cause text would be read as required parts, and since the title is cut at 100 characters those parts could be truncated.
findings.evidence: hestia.rs:1050-1053 builds the title as 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: {title}', where title is the first 100 characters of cause_text. The plan skips lines starting 'Cause:', 'Failure class:', 'Introspection ' and 'Priority:'. It does not skip the title line, which holds the same quoted cause. Fix: Also skip a line starting 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:'. Alternatively, skip any line whose text after the colon is a prefix of the 'Cause:' line. Pin the rule with a corpus case whose cause text holds '(1) .. (2) ..'.

findings.summary: A `N.` line after `Acceptance:` fits both the Enumerated kind (counted anywhere) and the Bullet kind (counted after the heading). The plan does not say which kind it gets, and the two kinds need different numbers of matching stems (2 and 1).
findings.evidence: Decision 3 says enumerated parts count 'anywhere', and that `-`, `*` and `N.` bullets count after `Acceptance:`. steward.rs:1579 already has a request with '1. It parses' under 'Acceptance:'. Fix: State that a line after `Acceptance:` is a Bullet only and is never counted twice, and add a parser unit test for it.

findings.summary: PART_FILLER is applied before the trailing 's' is dropped, so 'passes' becomes the stem 'passe' and is not filtered, while 'pass' is.
findings.evidence: The order in Decision 4 is: drop FUNCTION_WORDS, COMMON_WORDS and PART_FILLER, then drop a trailing `s`. The bullet 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' (hestia.rs:1047) therefore keeps 'passe'. Fix: Apply the filler and stop lists to both the bare word and the stem, or add 'passe' to the filler list. Pin the result in part_stems_worked_examples.

summary: Verdict: revise. I read the gate (checks.rs:475-551, 624), the stem code (topics.rs:156-215), has_phrase (surveys.rs:39), the root-cause and steward request builders (hestia.rs:1005-1061, steward.rs:515-594), the replay window and margin (replay.rs:130-169), the corpus fixtures (refusal_corpus.rs:160-298, 1320-1358, 1860-1920) and the test helpers in reading.rs. I grepped every caller of refusing_check, check_reading_acceptance and check_reading_text, and every 'Acceptance:' fixture. The plan fixes the cause where it starts: one new step placed last in `refusing_check`, so no existing case changes its refusing check, with a separate parser that leaves `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` alone. The helpers and seams it names all exist (`refuser_for`, `terms_reading`, `governed_reading`, `reading_source`, `replay_declaration`, `acceptance_check_names`, `generated_root_cause_request`). Its demonstrations would fail without the step. Its dependents list holds up: the 'Acceptance:' fixtures in hestia.rs tests only queue requests, and reading.rs:7396 and 7743 are refused earlier or only call check_defined_terms. Rejecting criteria that only reuse a part's subject is a sound answer to sibling parts covering each other. The one major problem is the negation list for criteria. It cancels any criterion that contains common words such as 'skipped', 'excluded', 'omitted' or 'deferred', even when the request part uses the same word. Correct readings would be refused, the error does not show why, and the shares that the replay measures would rise. Three smaller points: the title line of generated requests is not skipped, a `N.` line under Acceptance: has no single kind, and filler words are filtered before the trailing 's' is dropped.
